title: Rowset functions and reading files in Fabric
summary: Fabric Warehouse and the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint read files with OPENROWSET(BULK) over OneLake or ADLS URLs. A OneLake path is checked when the query is compiled. It must point to a file under <Workspace>/<Artifact>/<Subfolder>; otherwise the engine raises error 13836, even inside sp_describe_first_result_set. These engines reject the SQL Server rowset functions that reach other servers: OPENQUERY, OPENDATASOURCE, linked servers and four-part names. Treat the OLE DB provider form of OPENROWSET and OPENXML as unavailable. OPENJSON, STRING_SPLIT and GENERATE_SERIES exist. Watch the output column types and nested JSON that needs AS JSON. A multi-character STRING_SPLIT separator is not caught at compile time.

claims.statement: OPENQUERY is not supported. Fabric has no linked servers, so pass-through queries to a remote server cannot be written.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT * FROM OPENQUERY(remote_srv, 'SELECT 1 AS a') AS q
claims.sql_server: SQL Server runs the pass-through query on a configured linked server.
claims.alternative: Land the remote data as files in OneLake and read them with OPENROWSET(BULK ...). For another warehouse or lakehouse in the same workspace, use a three-part name.

claims.statement: OPENDATASOURCE is not supported. Ad hoc connection strings inside a query are rejected.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server allows it when 'Ad Hoc Distributed Queries' is enabled.
claims.alternative: Read exported files with OPENROWSET(BULK ...), or use three-part names within the workspace.

claims.statement: Four-part names (server.database.schema.object) do not work, because linked servers do not exist. Only three-part names to items in the same workspace resolve.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server resolves four-part names through a linked server.
claims.alternative: Use a three-part name database.schema.object for another warehouse or lakehouse endpoint in the same workspace.

claims.statement: The OLE DB provider form of OPENROWSET (provider name plus connection string, without BULK) should be assumed rejected. Only OPENROWSET(BULK ...) is confirmed to work.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT * FROM OPENROWSET('MSOLEDBSQL', 'Server=srv;Trusted_Connection=yes;', 'SELECT 1 AS a') AS r
claims.sql_server: SQL Server accepts the provider form when ad hoc distributed queries are enabled.
claims.alternative: Use OPENROWSET(BULK 'https://...') over files in OneLake or ADLS.

claims.statement: OPENROWSET(BULK) checks a OneLake URL when the query is compiled, not only when it runs. A path that does not resolve to a file under <Workspace>/<Artifact>/<Subfolder> is rejected with error 13836. As a result, a query with placeholder workspace or item names fails even in sp_describe_first_result_set, before any WITH clause or FORMAT option is checked.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT r.id FROM OPENROWSET(BULK 'https://onelake.dfs.fabric.microsoft.com/ws/lh.Lakehouse/Files/data/f.parquet', FORMAT = 'PARQUET') WITH (id int) AS r
claims.sql_server: In SQL Server, OPENROWSET(BULK) reads local or UNC file paths and needs a FORMATFILE or a SINGLE_BLOB/SINGLE_CLOB/SINGLE_NCLOB option.
claims.alternative: Use the real workspace and item path that the Fabric portal shows for the file, and check the query shape against a file that exists.

claims.statement: OPENXML should be assumed unavailable for XML shredding.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT * FROM OPENXML(1, '/root/row', 1) WITH (id int) AS x
claims.sql_server: SQL Server shreds XML with OPENXML after preparing a document handle.
claims.alternative: Convert the data to JSON and use OPENJSON, or parse it before loading.

claims.statement: OPENJSON without a WITH clause returns the columns key, value and type. key is nvarchar(4000) and value is nvarchar(max), so cast the values before comparing them or doing arithmetic.
In OPENJSON ... WITH, a nested object or array needs the column typed nvarchar(max) AS JSON. Without AS JSON, a scalar column that points at an object silently returns NULL.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT j.a FROM OPENJSON(N'{"a":{"b":1}}') WITH (a nvarchar(max) '$.a' AS JSON) AS j

claims.statement: An AS JSON column in OPENJSON ... WITH must be nvarchar(max). Any other type is a compile error.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT j.a FROM OPENJSON(N'{"a":{"b":1}}') WITH (a nvarchar(100) '$.a' AS JSON) AS j
claims.sql_server: SQL Server raises the same error.
claims.alternative: Declare the column as nvarchar(max) AS JSON.

claims.statement: STRING_SPLIT with a multi-character separator is not rejected at compile time. The value column takes the input's type and length, for example varchar(4) for the literal 'a||b'. A clean compile does not show that the split works: the separator is documented as a single character, so do not rely on '||'.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server documents the separator as a single character.
claims.alternative: Use REPLACE to turn the multi-character separator into one character first, or use REGEXP_SUBSTR.

claims.statement: STRING_SPLIT does not guarantee output order. To get the position, pass 1 as the third argument (enable_ordinal) and order by the ordinal column.
claims.sql_server: SQL Server 2022 supports enable_ordinal; without it, the order is not guaranteed.

claims.statement: GENERATE_SERIES exists and returns one column named value, typed like its arguments (int for int literals). Use it instead of recursive CTEs or number tables built from sys.objects.
